whoNeeds.title: Who Needs This?
whoNeeds.p1: If you employ someone to work in your household — cleaning, childcare, elderly care, cooking, gardening — you are legally required to register them with Social Security, regardless of how many hours they work.
whoNeeds.p2: This applies to any regular, recurring employment relationship. Even if someone comes just a few hours per week, if it is on a regular basis, you must formalize it.
whoNeeds.p3: Failing to register a domestic worker can result in fines from 3,126 EUR to 10,000 EUR, plus liability for any workplace accidents.

arraigo.title: Hiring a Worker Pending Arraigo / Residency
arraigo.intro: A common question from expat employers: 'My cleaning lady is undocumented but applied for arraigo. Can I register her with Social Security now?' Short answer: NO — but you are essential to her getting legal. Here is the actual sequence.
arraigo.whatIs: Arraigo is Spain's regularization pathway for undocumented residents who can prove integration ('roots'). Since November 2025, the requirement was reduced from 3 years to 2 years of continuous presence in Spain, and contracts of just 20 hours/week now qualify (instead of 30h/week) — specifically benefiting domestic workers.
arraigo.sequenceIntro: The order is inverted from what most people assume. You CANNOT register an undocumented worker with Social Security. Instead:
arraigo.step1: You sign a pre-contrato (pre-contract) committing to hire her as empleada de hogar for at least 1 year. This is NOT yet a real employment relationship — just a binding promise.
arraigo.step2: She submits the arraigo application using your pre-contract as proof of employability. You provide supporting documents (DNI/NIE, income proof, tax/SS clearance certificates).
arraigo.step3: Wait 3-6 months for the resolution. The administration has a maximum of 3 months to respond; silence means denial.
arraigo.step4: Permit granted — she receives her NIE with active work authorization (TIE card).
arraigo.step5: NOW you register her — Within 1 month of the permit approval, formalize the real contract and file the alta in IMPORT@SS. Use our Nomina Generator from this point onwards.
arraigo.multiEmployerTitle: Good News: You Do NOT Have to Hire Her Full-Time
arraigo.multiEmployerP1: The 20h/week threshold is COMBINED across all employers, not per employer. Your worker can present multiple contracts that together reach the threshold. Example: 8h/week with you + 8h/week with another family + 6h/week with an elderly care client = 22h total, which meets the requirement.
arraigo.multiEmployerP2: There is no minimum hours per single employer — contracts as low as 4h/week are valid as long as the combined total reaches 20h (arraigo sociolaboral, post-May 2025) or 30h (traditional arraigo social).
arraigo.multiEmployerP3: Each individual contract must still be at least 1 year in duration and pay at least the SMI proportional to hours (9.55 EUR/h in 2026). Each employer files a separate alta in Social Security when the permit is granted.
arraigo.multiEmployerExample: Practical example for your friend's situation:
arraigo.exampleTotal: Combined total: 22h/week — qualifies for arraigo sociolaboral
arraigo.whyTitle: Why You Cannot Register Her Now
arraigo.why: Social Security will reject any alta for someone without active work authorization. A NIE number alone is not enough — she needs a NIE with work permission. Filing for an undocumented worker is illegal and exposes you to fines from 10,001 EUR to 100,000 EUR per worker.
arraigo.req1: Clean tax record (al corriente with Hacienda and Seguridad Social)
arraigo.req2: Sufficient declared income to cover salary + employer SS contributions
arraigo.req3: Sign a pre-contract of at least 1 year duration
arraigo.req4: Commit to filing the alta within 1 month of permit approval
arraigo.doc1: Copy of your DNI or NIE/TIE
arraigo.doc2: Last 3-6 months of nominas OR last income tax return (Renta) showing solvency
arraigo.doc3: Certificate of being up-to-date with Hacienda (obtainable at sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es)
arraigo.doc4: Certificate of being up-to-date with Seguridad Social (obtainable at IMPORT@SS)
arraigo.doc5: Signed pre-contract (modelo oficial available from MITES)
arraigo.doc6: Padron certificate (your residency registration) showing household composition
arraigo.warning: Disclaimer: This is general guidance only. Arraigo applications can be complex and recent reforms have specific transitional rules. We strongly recommend consulting an immigration lawyer (abogado de extranjeria) for your specific case — most offer free initial consultations.

documentation.title: Documentation Needed
documentation.employer2: CCC (Codigo de Cuenta de Cotizacion) — your employer account with Social Security. See next section if you don't have one.
documentation.employer3: IBAN bank account — Social Security will auto-debit your monthly employer contributions from this account.
documentation.employer4: Digital Certificate or Cl@ve credentials — needed to access IMPORT@SS online portal.
documentation.worker1: DNI or TIE (Tarjeta de Identidad de Extranjero) with valid work authorization
documentation.worker2: Social Security Number (Numero de Afiliacion) — if they don't have one, you can request it during the registration process
documentation.worker3: IBAN bank account — for salary transfers (recommended but not legally required)

ccc.title: Getting Your Employer Code (CCC)
ccc.p1: The CCC (Codigo de Cuenta de Cotizacion) is your employer registration number with Social Security. You need one specifically for the 'Sistema Especial de Empleados de Hogar' (domestic workers special system).
ccc.p2: You can request it online through IMPORT@SS or in person at your nearest TGSS office.
ccc.online1: Go to IMPORT@SS portal and log in with your Digital Certificate or Cl@ve
ccc.online2: Navigate to 'Inscripcion del Empleador' or 'Solicitud de CCC'
ccc.online3: Select 'Sistema Especial de Empleados de Hogar' as the regime
ccc.online4: Enter your IBAN for SS direct debit
ccc.online5: You'll receive your CCC immediately or within 24-48 hours
ccc.inPerson1: Request an appointment at your nearest Tesoreria General de la Seguridad Social
ccc.inPerson2: Bring your DNI/NIE and IBAN details
ccc.inPerson3: Ask for 'inscripcion como empleador en el Sistema Especial de Empleados de Hogar'

contract.title: The Employment Contract
contract.p1: You must sign a written employment contract. While verbal contracts are technically legal for some arrangements, a written contract protects both parties and is strongly recommended.
contract.indefinido: Indefinite (Indefinido) — No end date. The most common and recommended type. Required if the employment is ongoing.
contract.temporal: Temporary (Temporal) — Fixed end date. Only valid for genuinely temporary situations (e.g., covering a leave of absence).
contract.porHoras: By Hours (Por Horas) — Specifies exact hours per week/month rather than full-time. Can be indefinite or temporary.
contract.key1: Working hours and schedule (e.g., 'Monday and Thursday, 9:00-13:00')
contract.key2: Salary (must meet or exceed the SMI for the agreed hours)
contract.key3: Whether extra pay (pagas extra) is prorated into the monthly salary or paid separately in June and December
contract.key4: 30 calendar days of paid vacation per year

registration.title: Registering with Social Security (Dar el Alta)
registration.p1: You must register your worker BEFORE their first day of work. This is done entirely online via IMPORT@SS.
registration.important: Important: Registering after the worker has already started is illegal and can result in penalties.
registration.step1: Log into IMPORT@SS with your Digital Certificate or Cl@ve
registration.step2: Go to 'Afiliacion, Altas y Bajas' > 'Alta de Trabajador en Empleados de Hogar'
registration.step3: Enter the worker's NIE/DNI and Social Security number
registration.step4: Specify the contract details: hours per month, salary, start date
registration.step5: Confirm your IBAN for the monthly SS direct debit

baseCotizacion.title: Understanding the Contribution Base (Base de Cotizacion)
baseCotizacion.p1: The Social Security contribution base for domestic workers is NOT the actual salary. Instead, the TGSS assigns a fixed bracket (tramo) based on the worker's reported monthly salary.
baseCotizacion.p2: This means your monthly SS payments are based on the tramo base, not the exact salary amount. Here are the 2026 brackets:
baseCotizacion.p3: After you register or update the salary in IMPORT@SS, the TGSS will assign the corresponding tramo. You can verify it on your monthly SS receipt.

monthly.title: Monthly Obligations
monthly.p1: Every month you have three obligations as an employer of a domestic worker:
monthly.obligation1: Transfer the net salary (gross minus worker SS deductions) to your worker. Keep a signed payslip (nomina) as proof.
monthly.obligation2: The TGSS automatically debits both the employer and worker contributions from your IBAN. This happens around the last day of the month for the current month's contributions.
monthly.obligation3: Give your worker a formal nomina each month showing: gross salary, deductions, net pay, and employer costs. Our Nomina Generator tool creates these for you.

vacation.title: Vacations & Leave
vacation.vacation1: 30 calendar days per year (or proportional if less than a full year).
vacation.vacation2: At least 15 consecutive days must be taken together.
vacation.vacation3: The schedule should be agreed between both parties. If no agreement, courts decide.
vacation.vacation4: For hourly contracts with the 9.55 EUR/h rate: vacation is already included in the rate. The worker still gets the time off, but it's already paid for.
vacation.sick1: The worker must provide a medical certificate (parte de baja) from their doctor.
vacation.sick2: Days 1-3: No payment obligation (unless your contract says otherwise).
vacation.sick3: Days 4-15: The employer pays 60% of the contribution base.
vacation.sick4: Day 16 onwards: Social Security pays directly (60% days 16-20, then 75%).
vacation.sick5: You must continue paying SS contributions during the sick leave.

termination.title: Termination & Finiquito
termination.p1: Ending the employment relationship requires following specific procedures:
termination.desistimiento1: You can end the contract at any time without cause, but you must:
termination.desistimiento2: Give 20 days advance notice (7 days if employment < 1 year)
termination.desistimiento3: Pay compensation of 12 days' salary per year worked
termination.desistimiento4: Grant 6 hours/week of paid time for job searching during the notice period
termination.despido1: If there is a valid cause (misconduct, breach of contract), you can dismiss without the 12-day compensation, but you must still provide notice.
termination.finiquito1: Upon termination, you must pay the finiquito which includes:
termination.finiquito2: Pending salary days of the current month
termination.finiquito3: Prorated extra pay (pagas extra) if not already prorated
termination.sepe: Remember to report the 'baja' (deregistration) in IMPORT@SS within 3 calendar days of the last working day.

modelo149.pageSubtitle: Prepare your Beckham Law application step by step. We explain every field so you can file with confidence on AEAT's website.
modelo149.savingsNote: Gestorias charge 500-1,500 EUR for this. Do it yourself for free.

whatIs.title: What is the Beckham Law?
whatIs.p1: The Beckham Law (officially: Regimen Especial de Trabajadores Desplazados) lets new residents in Spain pay a flat 24% income tax rate instead of the progressive scale (19-47%) for 6 years.
whatIs.p2: It applies to Spanish-sourced employment income up to 600,000 EUR. Above that, the rate is 47%. Foreign non-employment income (dividends, rental income from abroad) is largely exempt.
whatIs.p3: To apply, you file Modelo 149 with the Agencia Tributaria (AEAT) within 6 months of your Social Security registration.

eligibility.title: Am I Eligible?
eligibility.subtitle: Answer these questions to check if you qualify:
eligibility.q1: Have you been a NON-resident of Spain for the last 5 tax years?
eligibility.q2: Have you moved to Spain due to a job, business, or qualifying activity?
eligibility.q3: Did you register with Social Security less than 6 months ago?
eligibility.q4: Is your ownership in any Spanish company below 25%?
eligibility.resultYes: You likely qualify for the Beckham Law! Use the form below to prepare your Modelo 149.
eligibility.resultNo: Based on your answers, you may not qualify. Review the specific requirements below or consult a tax advisor.
eligibility.resultPartial: You may qualify but some conditions need verification. Review the details below.

deadline.title: When to Submit
deadline.p1: You must file Modelo 149 within 6 months of your Social Security registration date. This deadline is absolute — the Supreme Court confirmed that even one day late means permanent denial.
deadline.calculator: Enter your SS registration date to check your deadline:

documents.title: Required Documents
documents.p1: Before filing, you must upload supporting documents to AEAT's portal and get a registration code (CSV). You'll need this code for the form.
documents.all4: Certificate of non-residence in Spain for the last 5 years
documents.employment2: Employer certificate confirming start date and location

howToSubmit.title: How to Submit
howToSubmit.step1: Gather all required documents (see list above)
howToSubmit.step2: Go to AEAT sede electronica and upload your documents under 'Modelo 149 - Aportar documentacion'. Save the CSV registration code you receive.
howToSubmit.step3: Access the Modelo 149 form on sede electronica (requires digital certificate or Cl@ve)
howToSubmit.step4: Fill in each section using the preparation form below as your reference
howToSubmit.step5: Click 'Validar' then 'Firmar y Enviar' to submit
howToSubmit.step6: Download the proof of submission PDF. Resolution typically takes 2-8 weeks.

mistakes.title: Common Mistakes to Avoid
mistakes.m1: Missing the 6-month deadline — it is absolute and non-negotiable
mistakes.m2: Not uploading documents BEFORE filing — you need the CSV code first
mistakes.m3: Wrong start date — the clock starts from SS registration, not arrival
mistakes.m4: Director with 25%+ ownership — you are disqualified
mistakes.m5: Not filing Modelo 030 first — you may need AEAT registration before filing 149
mistakes.m6: Forgetting to notify your employer — they need to withhold at 24% flat
mistakes.m7: Not filing Modelo 151 annually — Beckham beneficiaries use 151, not 100

afterApproval.title: After Approval
afterApproval.a1: Provide the approval certificate to your employer for correct 24% withholding
afterApproval.a2: File annual tax returns using Modelo 151 (not the standard Modelo 100)
afterApproval.a3: Declare foreign assets over 50,000 EUR via Modelo 720
afterApproval.a4: Pay Wealth Tax on worldwide assets (Beckham does NOT exempt you from this)
afterApproval.a5: The regime lasts 6 years total (year of arrival + 5 more). After it ends, you cannot reapply for 5 years.

bajaMedica.pageSubtitle: When your empleada de hogar goes on baja medica, you must issue a C-133 certificate so she can claim her Social Security benefit. We walk you through the process and generate the form for you.

whatIs.title: What is the C-133?
whatIs.p1: The C-133 is the official Certificado del Empleador issued by the INSS. It certifies the employment relationship and contribution bases of a domestic worker so she can apply for Social Security benefits — most commonly for medical leave (incapacidad temporal), but also for childbirth/childcare, pregnancy risk, breastfeeding risk, or care of a seriously ill child.
whatIs.p2: Without a signed C-133 from each of her employers, the INSS cannot calculate her benefit. If she works for several households, every employer must issue one.
whatIs.p3: Important: the C-133 does NOT replace the parte de baja from her doctor — it is a separate document the worker must attach to her benefit application.

whoPays.title: Who Pays During Sick Leave?
whoPays.p1: While she is on sick leave, her contract is paused — you don't owe her the regular salary. Instead, an INSS benefit called IT (Incapacidad Temporal — 'Temporary Incapacity') replaces part of her income. For common illness or non-work injury, the split since the 2022 reform is:
whoPays.note: For workplace accidents or occupational illness (AT/EP), the INSS pays 75% directly from the day after the baja — there is no employer-paid window.
whoPays.continueSs: Even though salary is paused, you must keep paying the monthly Social Security contributions during the entire leave. Don't stop the direct debit.

employerSteps.title: What You (the Employer) Must Do
employerSteps.intro: There are 5 things you have to do once your worker hands you her parte de baja medica:
employerSteps.s1: Receive the parte de baja from the worker. The parte de baja is an official one-page document her doctor (medico de cabecera at her health centre) prints or sends digitally — it states the diagnosis category, the start date of the leave, and the expected duration. She keeps the original for the INSS; you keep a photo or photocopy for your own records (you'll need the start date).
employerSteps.s2: Fill in the C-133 with your data (DNI, CCC, address) and her data (NSS, NIE, contract type, tramo, dates). Use the form below to generate it. Then see the submission walkthrough for how to actually send it.
employerSteps.s3: Sign the C-133 and give a signed copy to the worker so she can attach it to her INSS application.
employerSteps.s4: Pay days 4-8 directly to the worker (60% of the base reguladora) on the next payday. Show it as a separate concept on the nomina, not as ordinary salary. See the worked example below.
employerSteps.s5: Keep paying SS contributions as usual via direct debit. Do not file a baja in IMPORT@SS — the contract is suspended, not terminated.

calculator.title: Calculator: how much will you pay?
calculator.intro: Type her monthly gross salary (or her hours/week and hourly rate) and we'll work out exactly what you owe her on days 4-8 — and what the INSS picks up after that. Numbers use 2026 rates.
calculator.summary: you'll transfer her about {amount} on the next nomina (a one-time amount, no matter how long the baja runs). After day 8, the INSS handles everything.

submit.title: How to Generate and Submit the C-133
submit.intro: Two parts: first you generate the form (step-by-step below), then you get it to the INSS (three submission options after that).

generate.title: Step-by-step: generate the C-133 with the form below
generate.intro: The wizard at the bottom of this page produces a fully-filled-in C-133 PDF. Here's what you'll fill in at each step:
generate.s1: Click the button below to jump to the form, then click "Next" through each step.
generate.s2: Step 1 — Benefit type: choose "Temporary incapacity (medical leave)". This is what your worker is claiming when she's on baja médica. (The other options are for childbirth, pregnancy risk, etc.)
generate.s3: Step 2 — Your data (employer): enter your name, DNI/NIE, and your CCC (Código de Cuenta de Cotización — find it on any nómina you've issued, or in IMPORT@SS under your employer profile). Then your home address and a phone number.
generate.s4: Step 3 — Worker data + dates: her full name, her NSS (the 12-digit Número de la Seguridad Social — on her TIE card or any of her nóminas), her DNI/NIE, contract type (full-time vs part-time/hourly — almost always part-time for empleadas de hogar), her tramo (look at her last nómina or your monthly SS receipt), the date she started working with you, and the first day of her parte de baja.
generate.s5: Step 4 — Contribution bases: add at least one row with the previous month's contribution base. The base appears on her last nómina under "Base de cotización" or on your TGSS monthly receipt. If she's part-time, add the three months prior. The form auto-suggests the base from her tramo — so usually you can just confirm.
generate.s6: Step 4 (continued) — Sign-line info: enter your locality (e.g. "Madrid"), today's day, month, and year. This goes on the C-133 signature line.
generate.s7: Step 5 — Review: click "Download PDF". Print it, sign it by hand on the line, and you have your C-133 ready to hand to her or submit yourself.

submit.submitIntro: Once the C-133 is signed, here are the three ways to get it to the INSS. Option A is by far the easiest.

optionA.title: Option A — She submits it (recommended, 90% of cases)
optionA.p1: The simplest path: you don't submit anything yourself. The C-133 is part of HER benefit application package — she attaches it as supporting documentation when she files her IT claim.
optionA.s1: Print the C-133 (or save the PDF), sign it, and hand a signed copy to your worker. Photo of the signed paper also works if she's filing online.
optionA.s2: She logs into sede.seg-social.gob.es with Cl@ve or her digital certificate.
optionA.s3: She finds the trámite "Solicitud de prestación por incapacidad temporal" (in the "Ciudadanos" → "Familia" / "Empleados de hogar" section).
optionA.s4: She fills in the application and uploads, as supporting documents: parte de baja + your signed C-133 + her DNI/NIE + IBAN. Done.

optionB.title: Option B — You submit it yourself online (if she can't)
optionB.p1: If she doesn't have a digital certificate or Cl@ve, you can submit the C-133 on her behalf via the generic document-upload trámite. This is the click-by-click path from sede.seg-social.gob.es:
optionB.s1: On the homepage, click "Ciudadanos" in the top tabs (or scroll to the "Ciudadanos" panel).
optionB.s2: In the left menu, click "Familia" → "Empleados del hogar". (Alternative: use the search box at the top, type "C-133" or "certificado del empleador".)
optionB.s3: Look for "Aportación de documentos a un trámite" or "Aportar documentos para una prestación" and click it.
optionB.s4: Authenticate with Cl@ve permanente or your certificado digital. (You can install Cl@ve in 10 minutes at clave.gob.es if you don't have it.)
optionB.s5: Reference the worker's NSS as the prestación holder, choose "Incapacidad temporal" as the trámite type, and upload the signed C-133 PDF.
optionB.s6: Save the justificante (receipt) PDF — it's your proof of submission. Forward a copy to the worker so she can reference it in her own application.

optionC.title: Option C — Without a digital certificate
optionC.p1: If neither of you has a digital certificate or Cl@ve, three offline channels work:
optionC.run: the government's no-certificate trámite portal — upload the C-133 with just your DNI
optionC.mail: Send the signed paper C-133 by certified mail (correo ordinario certificado) to the INSS office in your province
optionC.inPerson: Walk it into a Centro de Atención e Información de la Seguridad Social (CAISS) — book an appointment at 901 16 65 65 or 91 542 11 76 or via run.gob.es/trdcita

example.title: Worked Example: 8h/week Worker on a Full Month of Baja
example.intro: Concrete numbers for a worker who comes 8 hours per week (over 2 days), at the 2026 SMI of 9.55 EUR/h:
example.row1: Monthly gross salary: 8 h/week × 4.33 weeks × 9.55 EUR ≈ 331 EUR/month
example.row3: Daily base reguladora: 306 / 30 = 10.20 EUR/day (calendar days, not workdays)
example.split: If she's on baja for 30 calendar days, the 30 days are split like this:
example.d2: Days 4-8 (5 days, paid by you): 5 × 60% × 10.20 = 30.60 EUR ← what you pay her
example.d3: Days 9-20 (12 days, paid by INSS direct): 12 × 60% × 10.20 = 73.44 EUR (not your money)
example.d4: Days 21-30 (10 days, paid by INSS direct): 10 × 75% × 10.20 = 76.50 EUR (not your money)
example.summary: Your out-of-pocket: ~30.60 EUR for the days-4-8 window — a one-time fixed amount per leave, no matter how long she's out. After day 8, the INSS handles everything.
example.note: On top of that you keep paying the monthly Social Security contributions as usual (around 30-40 EUR for an 8h/week worker after bonifications). The IT cash benefit is calculated on the full base reguladora — not pro-rated by her actual workdays — because empleadas de hogar are paid by calendar day in the IT system, like any other worker.

workerSteps.title: What She (the Worker) Must Do
workerSteps.intro: She is responsible for filing the actual benefit claim. Her steps are:
workerSteps.s1: Get the parte de baja from her doctor and hand a copy to every employer within 3 days.
workerSteps.s2: Submit follow-up partes de confirmacion every 7 days (common illness) or as the doctor instructs.
workerSteps.s3: File the IT benefit application at the INSS within 15 calendar days of the baja, attaching: parte de baja + every employer's signed C-133 + her DNI/NIE + bank details for the payment.
workerSteps.s4: When she recovers, deliver the parte de alta to every employer the same day.
workerSteps.cta: Open Sede Electronica de la Seguridad Social

documents.title: Documents Checklist
documents.intro: What you both need to gather:
documents.d1: Parte de baja medica (from her doctor) — she gives a copy to you and keeps the original for the INSS
documents.d2: C-133 signed by you (one per employer if she has several)
documents.d3: Her DNI/NIE and Numero de Afiliacion a la Seguridad Social (NSS)
documents.d4: IBAN for the INSS to deposit the benefit

after.title: After She Returns
after.p1: Once she recovers and you receive the parte de alta:
after.a1: She returns to work the day after the alta
after.a2: Resume normal salary on the next nomina
after.a3: No need to re-register her in IMPORT@SS — the contract was never terminated

mistakes.title: Common Mistakes to Avoid
mistakes.m1: Filing a baja in IMPORT@SS — DO NOT. Sick leave suspends the contract; it does not end it. A baja means losing her job.
mistakes.m2: Stopping the SS direct debit — contributions continue during the entire leave
mistakes.m3: Not paying days 4-8 — the worker can claim them with interest plus penalties
mistakes.m4: Skipping the C-133 — without it, the INSS denies or delays her benefit indefinitely

reference.title: 2026 Reference: SMI + Tramos
reference.intro: Quick reference for the 2026 minimum wage and the contribution-base brackets the TGSS applies to empleados de hogar. Sourced directly from the BOE — these are the legally binding figures.
reference.smiHourlyHint: Hourly empleadas de hogar — already includes vacation + pagas extras prorated
reference.tramosIntro: TGSS does not contribute on the actual salary — it assigns a fixed monthly base from the bracket your worker's salary falls into. Add prorated pagas extras to her monthly pay before placing her on the scale.
reference.transitionNote: If your nómina shows different figures: some gestorías keep using 2025 values until they update their software for the 30 March 2026 order. Your TGSS direct debit will eventually regularize. For C-133 contribution bases, enter what was actually contributed each month (the figure on your nómina), not the 2026 BOE figure.
